primary_claim: Across 37 analyses and 153 pre-registered statistical tests on single-cell foundation models (scGPT, Geneformer), attention-based gene regulatory network extraction fails at every level that matters -- trivial gene-level baselines (AUROC 0.881) dominate attention/correlation-derived pairwise edges (~0.70), edges add ~zero incremental value (DeltaAUROC = -0.0004), and the attention heads most aligned with known regulation are the most dispensable under causal ablation -- while the models nonetheless learn real layer-organized biological structure (e.g. TRRUST regulatory signal peaking at layer 15, surviving expression residualisation) and activation patching in these models shows a large, formally quantifiable non-additivity bias that undermines standard single-component rankings.

effect.metric: AUROC for perturbation-response prediction; delta-AUROC incremental value; non-additivity residual ratio
effect.value: gene-level variance AUROC=0.881 vs attention/correlation edges ~0.70; adding attention edges to gene-level features DeltaAUROC=-0.0004 (n=559,720 pairs, power>99% to detect 0.005); ablating top TRRUST-ranked heads: zero significant degradation vs significant drop from random head ablation (23x larger logit perturbation confirmed via fidelity check); median non-additivity lower-bound ratio 0.725 across run-pairs

contradicts_or_qualifies: The field's implicit narrative (e.g. Theodoris et al. 2023, Cui et al. 2024) that attention patterns in biological transformers straightforwardly encode gene regulatory networks and that extraction is primarily an engineering problem

Prior independent benchmarks (Ahlmann-Eltze et al., Csendes et al., Wenteler et al., Bendidi et al., Chen & Zou) showing foundation models underperform simple baselines on perturbation prediction -- this paper's results are consistent with and extend that skeptical line
stated_future_work: Intervention-aware pretraining on perturbation/CRISPR screen data rather than purely observational expression data
Geometric/manifold-based interpretability (e.g. SAEs on residual stream) to look for regulatory structure invisible to attention extraction
Train linear probes on residual stream representations at each layer for specific regulatory relationships
Hybrid architectures using foundation model embeddings as inputs to dedicated GRN inference modules (e.g. GEARS) rather than extracting edges from attention
Extend CSSI with conformal prediction for certified edge sets with confidence guarantees
Test whether the non-additivity bias in activation patching generalizes to LLMs like GPT-2 or Llama
limitations_stated: Cannot fully resolve whether the failure is extraction failure (knowledge present but inaccessible) or knowledge absence (never learned); surface-capability evidence from prior literature is mixed
Non-additivity bias in activation patching demonstrated only in a 316M-parameter biological transformer, not in GPT-2, Llama, or other LLMs; magnitude in LLMs is an open question
RPE1 cell-type attention advantage decomposes into confound structure under the full test battery despite being statistically robust on its own
Per-TF regulatory signal trend (master regulators showing higher AUROC) did not survive multiple testing correction given small sample of evaluable TFs
quote: Attention-based gene regulatory network extraction fails at every level that matters, mostly because trivial gene-level baselines already explain the signal and the heads most aligned with known regulation turn out to be the most dispensable for the model's actual computation.
